context_quotes: With increasing the Sr- or Ba-concentration x, the system becomes metallic ferromagnet with rather large magnetic moments.
For R = Pr and Nd and A = Ca, the system approaches the metal-insulator phase boundary but does not become metallic.
The magnetic moments of the Ca-doped systems measured with the magnetic field H = 0.1 T are much smaller than those of the Ba- and Sr-doped systems.

The thermoelectric powers of the Ba- and Sr-doped systems decrease from large positive values of lightly doped samples to negative ones with increasing doping level, while those of Ca-doped systems remain positive.
These results can be understood by considering the relationship between the average ionic radius of R(1-x)A(x) and the energy difference between the low spin and intermediate spin states.
